則.meaning: A tiny <part>shellfish</part> at the bottom of a rock pool keeps a <part>dagger</part>, not for fighting but as a pen. Each night it scratches one line into the stone: 'The tide comes in twice.' 'Starfish nap at noon.' And the sea, oddly, does just what it says. Every line becomes a <kanji>rule</kanji>.
則.on: When the stone is full, it writes the newest one on a lost <sound>sock</sound> that drifted into the pool.
則.kun: It also ties one <sound>knot</sound> per rule in a strand of seaweed and winds it round a <sound>to</sound>tem pole on the shore, and the fish follow every one.

史.meaning: An ancient tortoise opens its <part>mouth</part> and tells tales of dinosaurs, kings and floods, while a tailor with <part>scissors</part> snips each tale into a ribbon and sews them end to end. The ribbon now wraps round the planet twice. That's the whole of <kanji>history</kanji>.
史.on: The oldest ribbon is pinned to a dented knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld from a battle long ago.

底.meaning: A boy drags his <part>sled</part> into the garden <part>shed</part>, climbs on and pushes off. The floorboards give way and he whooshes down a hidden slope, past the cellar, past the worms, past a buried pirate chest, until he bumps to a halt at the very <kanji>bottom</kanji>.
底.on: His mum lowers a roll of sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe down the hole, so he can climb back up.
底.kun: Down there someone has left a squashy <sound>so</sound>fa and a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala, so he stays a while.

敷.meaning: A fussy butler unfolds a tablecloth on the beach: he wafts it open with a <part>fan</part>, lets the wind fill it like a <part>sail</part>, and pins each corner with a <part>flyswatter</part>, until it covers the sand from the cliffs to the sea. The seagulls are delighted. He loves to <kanji>spread</kanji> things out.
敷.on: Next he unrolls a <sound>fu</sound>ton on top of it for his afternoon nap.
敷.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p wanders over and spreads itself out across the futon too.

易.meaning: A witch's <part>broom</part> refuses to fly at night, so she simply waits for the <part>sun</part> to rise, and the broom sweeps itself up into the sky with no spell at all. She reads the paper on the way to work. Flying has never been so <kanji>easy</kanji>.
易.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l hitches a ride on the bristles; it doesn't even have to wiggle.
易.kun: She knits on the way too, a scarf of <sound>ya</sound>rn finished before she lands, and feeds the eel a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

慣.meaning: A hedgehog's new boyfriend is a balloon. At first every hug makes his <part>heartbeat</part> thump, sure her spines will <part>pierce</part> him and he'll pop. A year later he dozes on her back without a care. He's quite <kanji>accustomed</kanji> to it now.
慣.on: For their anniversary she gives him a pink <sound>car</sound>nation, holding the stem very carefully.
慣.kun: They share a warm <sound>na</sound>an, and he no longer flinches when she reaches for it.

厳.meaning: Teenagers plan a <part>daring</part> stunt: <part>fireworks</part> off the edge of the <part>cliff</part>. Then Granny steps out of the fog with her arms folded, and one look makes the matches droop in their hands. Her face is so <kanji>stern</kanji> the rockets fizzle out by themselves.
厳.on: Only <sound>Gen</sound>, the hiker from the valley, dares to ask if he may light just one.
厳.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' sighs Gen, pulls off his <sound>go</sound>ggles and sits on a <sound>so</sound>fa by the cliff edge, still and grave: solemn.

福.meaning: A shy <part>lamppost</part> keeps a <part>cookie jar</part> at its foot. Whoever walks home late and lifts the lid finds a warm cookie and a lucky penny inside. Nobody ever sees who fills it, but the whole street calls it a <kanji>blessing</kanji>.
福.on: The jar hangs from a big brass <sound>hook</sound> on the post, so the foxes can't reach it.

荒.meaning: A herd of party goats stampedes through a quiet meadow. They eat every blade of <part>grass</part>, use a mossy <part>tombstone</part> as a scratching post and drink the <part>river</part> down to mud. All they leave behind is one paper hat. The meadow is <kanji>laid waste</kanji>.
荒.on: On top of the mud sits a half-eaten ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, still dripping.
荒.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' wails the farmer when she sees it, and the goats trot off to wreck the next field.

賛.meaning: A <part>husband</part> brings home a giant <part>shellfish</part> he wants to keep as a pet. His wife frowns, the kids hold their breath, and the shellfish opens its shell and sings a little song. She melts and nods. Even she has to <kanji>approve</kanji>.
賛.on: To celebrate, the whole family shares a huge <sound>sun</sound>dae with the shellfish.
賛.kun: It helps out at home in return, carrying a <sound>ta</sound>co and a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi to the table.

硬.meaning: On the <part>night watch</part>, a guard stands so still on a <part>stone</part> wall that pigeons nest in his helmet and a spider spins a web between his boots. At dawn his captain taps him: he's frozen solid. His legs are too <kanji>stiff</kanji> to march home.
硬.on: His friend brings breakfast, an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, and that freezes solid too.
硬.kun: Down in the yard, a <sound>ca</sound>rp is stuck in a <sound>tu</sound>b of ice, just as hard.

群.meaning: A tiny <part>mister</part> in a bowler hat tries to cross a field, but a <part>sheep</part> follows him, then another, then three hundred more. He stops; they stop. He tiptoes; they tiptoe. Now he can't go anywhere without his woolly <kanji>flock</kanji>.
群.on: Big <sound>Gun</sound>ther the sheepdog sulks at the gate: that used to be his job.
群.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se wanders over, sees the crowd and decides to join them.

儀.meaning: Once a year the town hangs the old scales of <part>justice</part> on a golden <part>coat hook</part> in the square. A choir sings while the mayor dusts them with a feather, and nobody remembers why. It's simply the yearly <kanji>ceremony</kanji>.
儀.on: Then the clock tower's big <sound>gea</sound>r clunks round, and the bells ring to end it.

陣.meaning: A family drives their <part>car</part> into a field, ties a <part>pennant</part> to the aerial and declares it their castle. They build walls of deckchairs, dig a moat round the kettle and post the dog on guard. By dusk it's a proper battle <kanji>camp</kanji>.
陣.on: Supper is a stew with far too much <sound>gin</sound>ger in it, and the dog sneezes all night.

究.meaning: A rabbit professor has spent <part>nine</part> years down one <part>hole</part>, measuring roots, labelling worms and scribbling notes on the walls. When she finally pops up, she has a thousand pages about carrots. That's serious <kanji>research</kanji>.
究.on: She tests every root by tapping it with a pool <sound>cue</sound>.
究.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird reads all thousand pages and gasps '<sound>Wah</sound>!' She has taken carrots as far as they go: mastered.

研.meaning: A grumpy athlete keeps tripping over the <part>hurdle</part>, so she sits down with a <part>stone</part> and rubs the bar for hours until it gleams like a mirror. She still trips, but now she can watch her face as she falls. At least she knows how to <kanji>polish</kanji>.
研.on: Then she polishes the dog's <sound>ken</sound>nel too, until the dog needs sunglasses.
研.kun: Next she sharpens the top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole into a pencil point.

迎.meaning: Two rubber stamps, the <part>twin stamps</part>, wait at the foot of the hotel's <part>ramp</part>. Every guest who rolls down it gets a stamp on each hand: a smiley face and a heart. Even the suitcases get one. That's their idea of a <kanji>welcome</kanji>.
迎.on: A pressure <sound>gau</sound>ge by the door counts the guests, and its needle spins with joy.
迎.kun: Tonight they welcome a <sound>moo</sound>se and a <sound>ca</sound>rp in a fishbowl, and stamp them both.

委.meaning: A <part>woman</part> can't decide what to bake with her sack of <part>grain</part>, so she asks twelve neighbours to sit round her kitchen table and vote. They argue about bread versus cake for six hours, then order pizza. That's a <kanji>committee</kanji> for you.
委.on: One member, an <sound>ee</sound>l in a bucket, votes for every option at once.
委.kun: In the end she entrusts the sack to a <sound>yu</sound>zu farmer and his <sound>du</sound>ck, who bake it into one big loaf.

善.meaning: A huge <part>sheep</part> could easily bully the whole flock. Instead it opens its <part>mouth</part> only to say kind things, shares its grass and helps lambs over the fence. Even the wolves feel bad around it. It's the most <kanji>virtuous</kanji> sheep alive.
善.on: It spends its evenings raking a <sound>zen</sound> garden for the old ewes.
善.kun: It leaves a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt on every doorstep, just to be good.

採.meaning: A bored pirate lowers his <part>anchor</part> into a sunken casino and fishes about. Up comes a pair of <part>dice</part>, then a top hat, then a whole roulette wheel. He lays it all out on deck and lets the crew <kanji>pick</kanji> one thing each.
採.on: The cabin boy picks a dusty jug of <sound>ci</sound>der and drinks the lot.
採.kun: The captain takes a carved <sound>to</sound>tem pole from the wreck and props it by the wheel.

燃.meaning: A baby dragon practises his <part>fire</part> on a pile of logs. Nothing. He huffs, '<part>So</part> what,' turns away and sneezes, and the logs, the tent and Granny's armchair all whoosh up at once. Now everything has started to <kanji>burn</kanji>.
燃.on: Last to catch is Granny's washing line of crisp bed li<sound>nen</sound>, glowing orange.
燃.kun: Granny beats out the flames with her <sound>mo</sound>ccasin and grounds him for a week.

床.meaning: A <part>tree</part> grows up through the floor of a garden <part>shed</part>, so the gardener stops fighting it. He slings a hammock between two branches, piles moss on the lowest bough and tucks himself in. It's the comfiest <kanji>bed</kanji> he's ever had.
床.on: Birds in the branches put on a dawn <sound>show</sound> every morning to wake him.
床.kun: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole in the corner keeps watch, and a <sound>ko</sound>ala shares his pillow.

己.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> at the zoo rears up in front of a mirror and sways, trying to charm the snake it sees there. The other snake sways right back, every time. After three days the keeper explains that it's looking at its own <kanji>self</kanji>.
己.on: Next door, a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala laughs so hard it falls off its branch.
己.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, <sound>no</sound>,' hisses the cobra, blushing bright <sound>re</sound>d at its own reflection.

販.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> at the harbour market can't sell a single pearl, because his sign says '<part>anti</part>-pearl'. A clever crab rewrites it: 'Rare! Shiny! Only three left!' and the queue snakes round the harbour. That's the magic of <kanji>marketing</kanji>.
販.on: Next week the crab sells <sound>hon</sound>ey the same way, in pearl-shaped jars.

秘.meaning: A farmer hides a love letter inside one stalk of <part>grain</part> in a field of thousands. He's <part>certain</part> nobody will ever find it, so he tells no one, not even his dog. Only the scarecrow saw him. Now the two of them share a <kanji>secret</kanji>.
秘.on: He hides a map to the right stalk in a secret drawer in the <sound>hee</sound>l of his boot.
秘.kun: The scarecrow keeps it to himself, though now and then a giggle slips out: '<sound>Hee</sound>!'

宝.meaning: A magpie sneaks onto a <part>roof</part> and hides one <part>jewel</part> under a loose tile, then a spoon, a bottle cap and a wedding ring. When the roofer lifts the tile, the sparkle nearly blinds him. It's the magpie's <kanji>treasure</kanji>.
宝.on: He rinses the hoard with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se, and it gleams even brighter.
宝.kun: Underneath lie a <sound>ta</sound>co shell and a tin <sound>ca</sound>rp, and the magpie screeches '<sound>Rah</sound>!' when he touches them.

執.meaning: A puppy finds a <part>round</part> ball and won't let go. You can tug, shake, even offer him a steak, and he just wags with pure <part>happiness</part>, jaws locked tight. Nothing will make him drop it. He's very <kanji>tenacious</kanji>.
執.on: At bedtime he drags the ball under his <sound>shee</sound>t and growls at anyone who comes near.
執.kun: He keeps hold of it at the vet's, halfway up a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, even in his dreams.

灯.meaning: On a dark <part>street</part>, a firefly gets tired of flying about, so it moves into a glass jar on top of the signpost and keeps its tiny <part>fire</part> burning all night. Moths queue up for a chat. The street now has its own <kanji>lamp</kanji>.
灯.on: A late walker stubs his <sound>toe</sound> on the post and thanks the firefly for the light.
灯.kun: The firefly giggles '<sound>Hee</sound>!' and glows a little brighter.

巡.meaning: A tortoise in a police cap trundles up and down the <part>ramp</part> outside the school, waving a sign at every car that roars into the <part>speed zone</part>. Round and round he goes, all day, at one inch an hour. He takes his <kanji>patrol</kanji> very seriously.
巡.on: He hides behind a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush to catch the speeders.
巡.kun: Each lap, he stops for a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon from a <sound>goo</sound>die bag tied to his shell.

責.meaning: The TV goes fuzzy during the big match, and the whole family turns to glare at the <part>shellfish</part> perched on the roof, chewing the <part>TV antenna</part>. It looks guilty, but it was the pigeon. The shellfish still gets all the <kanji>blame</kanji>.
責.on: Dad draws a pie chart: one thin <sound>sec</sound>tor for the pigeon, the rest for the shellfish.
責.kun: Even the red <sound>se</sound>tter barks at it, though the dog slept through the whole thing.
